title: Device-Level Security Hardening (IOS XE)
levelTitle: Level 28 - Cisco IOS and IOS XE

cards.q: What is device-level security hardening on IOS XE?
cards.a: It protects the management and control plane of the device itself, covering login/AAA security, role-based access, control-plane policing (CoPP), SNMP management, and management-plane protection using least privilege.

cards.q: What are the three functions of AAA?
cards.a: Authentication verifies who the user is, authorization determines what they may do, and accounting logs what they did.

cards.q: What is the difference between TACACS+ and RADIUS?
cards.a: TACACS+ runs on TCP 49, separates authentication, authorization, and accounting, and encrypts all three, while RADIUS runs on UDP 1812/1813, combines authentication and accounting, and encrypts only the password.

cards.q: What is the difference between CoPP and management-plane protection?
cards.a: CoPP (control-plane policing) rate-limits control-plane traffic to stop DoS, while management-plane protection (MPP) restricts which management protocols and interfaces can be used for management.

cards.q: Why should management use SSH instead of Telnet?
cards.a: SSH encrypts the management session and credentials, while Telnet is cleartext and vulnerable to interception; restrict vty lines with transport input ssh.

cards.q: Why is enable secret preferred over enable password?
cards.a: enable secret stores the privileged password using a strong hash, while enable password is weak and can be stored in cleartext.

cards.q: How is least privilege implemented for local users?
cards.a: By assigning privilege levels (0-15) or roles/parser views so users only get the command access they need, rather than full privileged-mode access.

cards.q: How is CoPP configured on IOS XE?
cards.a: Create a class-map for the control-plane traffic, a policy-map with police cir actions, then apply it under the control-plane mode with service-policy input.

cards.q: Which commands verify AAA, SSH, and CoPP state?
cards.a: show aaa, show run aaa, show ip ssh, show control-plane, and show snmp.

cards.q: An administrator can no longer log in after tightening the vty lines; what is likely wrong?
cards.a: An ACL on the vty lines or transport input setting may be blocking the administrator's source address or protocol; check the line vty configuration and the applied access-class.

cards.q: What is a common hardening misconception about RADIUS?
cards.a: That RADIUS encrypts all traffic; RADIUS encrypts only the password, whereas TACACS+ encrypts the entire exchange and separates AAA functions.

cards.q: What is the hardening quick-review summary?
cards.a: Harden via AAA (TACACS+ vs RADIUS), least-privilege local users with enable secret, SSH instead of Telnet, CoPP for the control plane, MPP for the management plane, SNMPv3, and disabling unencrypted HTTP.
